- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots downward — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0 to +0.30), model tends to overestimate mean — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling >2% from peak), model often fails to recognize — add 1–3% downward bias in next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often delays correction — anticipate 1–2 day lag in upward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days of sentiment are negative, model tends to overestimate recovery — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 7–14 days.
